subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native OpenClaw trust/provenance model should govern durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, session memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, durable schema/migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and how external MCP/plugin implementations relate to native memory.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

options.title: Split To Foundations First
options.body: Make durable provenance foundations canonical first, then keep this issue as the trust-policy layer that depends on that contract.

options.title: Rely On External MCP
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp and similar integrations as optional user paths, leaving native OpenClaw memory without trust policy for now.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has both prior review context on this issue and feature-history ownership on the memory host/plugin boundaries that need product/security direction.
